title: Advanced Backpack Feature Explorer with Scoring System
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D backpack feature explorer using Three.js. The scene uses a robot model as a mascot/guide. Generate a complete HTML file with embedded JavaScript.

## Scene Setup
- Initialize a Three.js scene with a gradient background (dark blue #1a1a2e to #16213e).
- Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls with damping enabled, limited polar angle (0.3 to 1.4 radians), and min/max distance (3, 8).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from (5, 5, 5) intensity 0.8 and another from (-3, 3, -3) intensity 0.4.
- Load 'robot.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at position (0, 0, 0). Scale it to fit nicely (scale 1.0). The robot represents the backpack product mascot.
- Create a circular platform (CylinderGeometry, radius 2, height 0.1) beneath the model with metallic material (#2a2a4a).

## Feature Hotspots
- Create 5 clickable hotspot spheres (SphereGeometry, radius 0.12) placed around the robot model at different positions:
  1. 'Ergonomic Straps' - position (-0.5, 1.5, 0.3), color #ff6b6b
  2. 'Waterproof Pocket' - position (0.4, 1.0, 0.4), color #4ecdc4
  3. 'Laptop Compartment' - position (0, 0.8, -0.3), color #45b7d1
  4. 'USB Charging Port' - position (0.5, 1.3, 0.2), color #f9ca24
  5. 'Anti-Theft Zipper' - position (-0.3, 0.5, 0.4), color #a55eea
- Each hotspot should pulse (scale oscillation between 0.8 and 1.2 using sine wave).
- Hotspots should be raycasted on click.

## Feature Info Panel (DOM)
- Create a styled info panel (div, id='info-panel') positioned at right side of screen, initially hidden (display:none).
- When a hotspot is clicked, show the panel with feature name, description, and a star rating (1-5 stars).
- Each feature has a description: Ergonomic Straps='Padded mesh straps with load distribution', Waterproof Pocket='IPX7 rated sealed compartment', Laptop Compartment='Fits up to 17 inch laptops with padding', USB Charging Port='Built-in 10000mAh power bank connection', Anti-Theft Zipper='Hidden reverse coil zippers'.
- Include a 'Rate This Feature' section with 5 clickable star buttons (ids: star-1 through star-5).

## Scoring System
- Track an exploration score. Each new feature discovered adds 20 points (max 100 for all 5).
- Track ratings given: store each feature's rating.
- Display score in a HUD element (div, id='score-hud') at top-left showing 'Score: X / 100'.
- When all 5 features are explored, show a 'completion-badge' div with text 'Explorer Badge Earned!'.
- Add a 'Reset' button (id='reset-btn') that resets all scores, ratings, hides panels.

## Auto-Rotate Toggle
- Add a button (id='auto-rotate-btn') that toggles auto-rotation of the model platform and robot together. Default: OFF. When ON, rotate Y axis at 0.01 rad/frame.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true after robot.glb loads)
  - featuresDiscovered: number (0-5, count of unique features clicked)
  - discoveredFeatures: array of strings (names of discovered features)
  - currentFeature: string|null (currently displayed feature name)
  - score: number (0-100)
  - ratings: object mapping feature name to rating number (1-5)
  - totalRatings: number (count of features that have been rated)
  - autoRotate: boolean
  - allDiscovered: boolean (true when all 5 found)
  - panelVisible: boolean
  - hotspotCount: number (always 5)
  - cameraDistance: number (updated each frame, distance from camera to origin)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame and on every user interaction.
physics_constraints: Hotspots must pulse smoothly with sine-based oscillation. Camera orbit must be constrained within specified polar angle and distance limits. Auto-rotation must be consistent at 0.01 rad/frame when enabled. Score must never exceed 100 or go below 0. Ratings must be integers 1-5.
